_comment: Data Foundation Agent configuration. Edit values here — no code changes needed.

consistency._comment: Cross-field logical rules. A record can be in-range on every field yet still be physically self-contradictory — these catch that.

quality_score._comment: Six DAMA data-quality dimensions. Weights must sum to 1.0. Adjust to reflect what matters most for your historian feed.

dimension_labels.asset_mapping: Integrity — asset found in master table
dimension_labels.bearing_mapping: Integrity — bearing + channel found and matched
dimension_labels.completeness: Completeness — all critical signal fields present
dimension_labels.ranges_valid: Validity / Conformity — values within sensor bounds

dimension_descriptions.asset_mapping: Referential integrity of the asset key. The asset_id must resolve to a row in the asset master (Table 3); without it no asset context (line, criticality, downtime cost) can be joined and the record cannot be routed. Hard requirement.
dimension_descriptions.bearing_mapping: Referential integrity of the bearing key. The bearing_id and channel_id must both resolve to the same bearing master row (Table 2); a mismatch means a mis-labelled sensor channel. Hard requirement.
dimension_descriptions.completeness: Fraction of critical signal fields that are populated (not null). Measures how much of the expected payload actually arrived from the historian. Scored continuously: 1.0 minus the share of missing critical fields.
dimension_descriptions.ranges_valid: Conformity of each value to its physical / sensor operating bounds (rpm, load %, vibration, temperature, kurtosis floor, non-negative band energies). Per-bearing bounds from the master take priority over config fallbacks. Catches scaling errors, dead channels and impossible readings.
dimension_descriptions.accuracy: Trustworthiness of the reading as reported by the historian's own signal_quality_score (0–1), a proxy for sensor fidelity (cable noise, dropout, saturation). Scored as that value directly; below the quality floor it signals a likely sensor fault.
dimension_descriptions.consistency: Whether independent fields tell the same physical story — e.g. a 'running' state with near-zero rpm, or a stopped machine still reporting strong vibration. Catches contradictions that per-field range checks cannot see.

improvement_hints.bearing_mapping: Register the bearing_id and channel_id in bearing_master.json (Table 2)
improvement_hints.completeness: Ensure historian publishes all critical fields: vib_rms_mm_s, kurtosis, temp_c, bpfo_energy, bpfi_energy
improvement_hints.ranges_valid: Check sensor calibration and scaling factors in the historian configuration
improvement_hints.accuracy: Inspect the sensor cable and junction-box connection; a low signal_quality_score usually means a noisy, loose or failing transducer
improvement_hints.consistency: Reconcile the operating-state, speed and vibration tags — confirm the historian is reading rpm, machine_state and vibration from the same asset at the same instant

remediation._comment: Controls what happens to a FLAGGED record with missing fields. 'default_action' is used for unattended runs; a human (CLI prompt now, frontend later) can override it per record. A field is imputable ONLY if it appears in 'imputable_fields', which maps the signal field to the bearing-master baseline used to fill it. Identity fields can never be imputed.

fallback_sensor_bounds._comment: Used only when BearingMaster has no bounds for a given bearing. Per-bearing bounds in bearing_master.json take priority.
